sources.entry: PiPTool - Add the Picture-in-Picture Functionality to YouTube, Netflix, Plex and other video broadcasting services in macOS.

summary.one_liner: PiPTool is a Safari 10 extension that adds Picture-in-Picture to video players on sites like YouTube, Netflix, Plex and DailyMotion that Safari does not support natively.
summary.what_it_does: The extension targets video players that lack HTML5 Picture-in-Picture support, such as YouTube and DailyMotion, so Safari can show a PiP button for them. It includes a menu button that enables a picker mode: the user hovers over page elements (the hovered element gets a red border) and clicks a video to trigger PiP manually. The changelog mentions support for Netflix and Plex, plus a settings panel in Safari's Extensions preferences where extra Plex domains (including IP addresses) can be added. Supported sites are only triggered on the listed services, per the changelog. The README describes a Grunt-based build that outputs Safari extension files.
use_cases: Picture-in-picture video on YouTube in Safari
Pop out DailyMotion videos while browsing
Watch Netflix or Plex in a floating window on macOS
Manually pick a video on a web page to float it
Keep a video playing over other apps in Safari
how_to_run: Download the extension from the link in the README (link not provided in the text)
Run grunt live for development or grunt build to generate Safari files
notable: Adds Picture-in-Picture to sites like YouTube and DailyMotion that lack native HTML5 PiP in Safari
Menu button picker mode to choose any video on a page and open it in PiP
Configurable extra Plex domains via Safari Extensions settings
Triggers only on supported websites to improve performance
caveats: Built for Safari 10; the README does not state support for newer Safari versions
Building the .safariextz file requires Safari; the build command only generates the files
Known bug: the video stops when leaving picture-in-picture mode
